_README: harness - per-tool entries for the hybrid recency reminder.
This file IS the `{{TOOL_ENTRIES}}` block that proxy/reminder.md injects on
every turn: the legend line, plus one entry per tool in this turn's toolset.
Edit it freely: it is data, not code. `harness restart` reloads it (the proxy
reads it once at startup).
Keys (every key is optional; a missing or malformed one falls back on its own,
so a typo in one description never costs you the rest of the file):
legend            The sentence above the tool list. Teaches the model to
read `name(required, [optional])`.
state_check_note  Appended to the legend ONLY when a tool in this turn's
toolset is flagged `state_check` in some MCP's
recency.json. Set it to "" to suppress.
tool_search_note  Appended to the legend ONLY when cooperative tool-search
is on (HARNESS_TOOL_SEARCH=1). Set it to "" to suppress.
detail_tools      Tools whose FULL upstream description is echoed verbatim,
indented, under their own entry. Reserve this for tools
whose valid argument VALUES are an unguessable closed set
(`task`'s agent names, `skill`'s skill names) - the
descriptions are large and every one spends context.
tools             tool name -> the one-line guidance rendered after the
signature as `- name(args) - <guidance>`. Aim at the
failure mode the model still hits with the full schema in
context, not at re-describing the tool.
A tool with no entry here renders as a bare `- name(args)`, so deleting a
description is a supported edit, and an entry for a tool this turn does not
ship simply never renders. Guidance for an MCP server's tools does NOT belong
here: those are `<server>_<tool>` and live in that MCP's own recency.json
(see architecture/mcp.md). This map is consulted first; recency.json is the
fallback.
Keys starting with `_` are ignored by the loader, so this block costs nothing
at runtime. If the whole file is unreadable or is not a JSON object, the proxy
logs a loud `[!]` and falls back to a minimal built-in legend with no per-tool
guidance - tool calling keeps working, the hints go quiet.
Note: proxy/test_proxy.py, tests/proxy_test.sh and tests/scheme_contract_test.sh
assert on parts of this wording. Rewrite freely for your own use; expect those
tests to fail until you update them too.
legend: Tools — one entry per tool, all info for a tool in one place (signature, guidance, and any closed-set argument values). Full schemas are at <<<BEGIN_AGENT_TOOLS>>>. Signature format: name(required, [optional]); bracketed = optional; names not listed are unavailable; parameter names must match exactly (e.g. `filename` fails where `filePath` is required).
state_check_note: A tool marked [state-check] mutates state — before calling it, call the server's read-only state/orientation tool first to see current state; don't mutate blind.
tool_search_note: You can also call tool_list() to list every tool, or tool_search({"query": "..."}) to fetch a tool's full signature and description on demand.

tools.apply_patch: Apply a multi-file diff in one envelope. Wrap in `*** Begin Patch` / `*** End Patch`. Each file needs an `Add File:`/`Update File:`/`Delete File:` header. Existing files must be `read` first, same as `edit`.
tools.bash: Run a shell command (terminal: git, npm, docker, etc.). Pass `description` (short verb phrase). Use `workdir`, not `cd <dir> && …`. For file ops use read/edit/write, not cat/sed/echo.
tools.edit: Exact-string replacement in a file. `read` the file first. `oldString` must occur exactly once — add surrounding context or pass `replaceAll: true`. Do not include the `N: ` line-number prefix in `oldString`/`newString`.
tools.glob: Find files by name pattern (e.g. `**/*.ts`), sorted by mtime. For file *contents* use `grep`. Batch independent patterns in parallel.
tools.grep: Regex search across file contents (not names). Use `include` to scope (`"*.ts"`). For match counts use `bash` + `rg`.
tools.lsp: Language-server operations (defs, refs, hover, symbols). `line` and `character` are 1-based. Use only when you need symbol-level navigation; for plain text search, `grep`/`glob` are faster.
tools.plan-enter: Switch into the plan agent. Only call when the user has actually asked to plan; not for simple/direct asks.
tools.plan-exit: Switch out of the plan agent into build. Only call after the plan file is complete and the user is ready to implement.
tools.question: Ask the user a clarifying question with options. Ask BEFORE acting, not after. Don't ask for info the user has already supplied this turn.
tools.read: Read a file (or list a directory) by absolute path. Param is `filePath`, not `filename`/`path`. Prefer one larger read over many small re-reads.
tools.repo_clone: Clone an external repo into opencode's cache. For *external* repos only — your working dir is already mounted. The cache is read-only research material; don't try to modify it.
tools.repo_overview: Summarise structure/entrypoints of a cloned repo. Run after `repo_clone` to orient. Don't re-call within the same task.
tools.skill: Load a named skill's instructions into context. `name` must match exactly one of the skills listed below (closed set).
tools.task: Launch a sub-agent. `subagent_type` must match the closed list below. A sub-agent does NOT share your context — it starts blind, so write a self-contained, detailed prompt: state the goal, the relevant files/paths, the constraints, and exactly what to return. Sub-agent output is invisible to the user — summarise it back. Launch independent agents in parallel (multiple calls in one message), but spawn at most 8 at a time.
tools.todowrite: Maintain a structured todo list across the turn. Each item is `{content, status, priority}` — `priority` is the string `'high'`/`'medium'`/`'low'` (NOT an int, NOT omitted), `content` is the task text (NOT `description`/`subject`), `status` is `'pending'`/`'in_progress'`/`'completed'`/`'cancelled'`. Every call REPLACES the whole list, so always send every item, not just the changed one. Exactly ONE item may be `in_progress`. Flip an item to `completed` immediately after finishing it — not at end-of-turn, and not in the same call that starts it. This list is your memory. Your conversation history can be truncated at any point, and the reminder replays this list back to you afterwards — so keep it detailed and current, and write one for any task past a single trivial step.
tools.webfetch: Fetch a URL and convert to markdown/text/html. Read-only. If the fetch fails or is empty, say so — never invent the page contents.
tools.websearch: Live web search via the session's web search provider. Use the current year in queries (avoid stale-year framing). If you already have the URL, prefer `webfetch`.
tools.write: Create or overwrite a file at a path. If the file already exists you must `read` it first or the call fails. Don't create README/docs files unless asked.
